long_biography.plain_text:
In 1992, mining-equipment entrepreneur Fred Moir proposed a drilling system that would use high-pressure water to break hard rock while suppressing dust. He commissioned engineer Malcolm McInnes to develop it. Underground trials showed promise, but vibration reduced performance as the holes became deeper. McInnes responded with a redesigned impact drill, supported by a competitive government research grant.

Moir retained an interest in developing the technology after the sale of SDS, acquiring Impact Drilling International with other shareholders. The business became Specialised Drilling Services Australia, with Moir as chairman and principal shareholder. Its later Genie prototype underwent field trials in the Canadian Rockies.
